blocks.note: the foot of something is its end, as in the foot of the bed
a pad is informal for a flat or home

explanation.surface: An elderly crook is lying low in a flat at the end of the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A footpad was a highway robber on foot, a thief of earlier centuries rather than today.

clue.text: Iron, with gold and silver, found in raid

indicators.note: metals found in another are lodged inside it, so the first two sit within the iron

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
or is the heraldic word for gold
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Precious metals were recovered when police raided a premises.
explanation.walkthrough: Or is the heraldic term for gold; the gold and silver together are what sits within the iron.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to search widely, and as a noun it is a raid or foray for supplies.

blocks.note: something exposed is out in the open
an act of parliament is a law

explanation.surface: A robber is unmasked by something he did.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlaw is a fugitive criminal living beyond the law, as a bandit does.

clue.text: Publicity given polite look, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the words are to be judged by sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: proper means correct and polite in manner
a gander is informal for a look, as in take a gander

explanation.surface: A celebrity gets attention by giving someone a courteous glance.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in a non-rhotic British accent, proper gander sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is information spread to promote a cause, a kind of publicity.

blocks.note: a dig is a poke or jab
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to poke something with a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: Digit is the formal word for a finger or toe.

indicators.note: a fish in a belly is swallowed and held inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a pod is a slang word for a paunch or pot belly
the char is a trout-like freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A bird has swallowed a fish, which now sits in its stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: Belly here is a pot belly or paunch, not the stomach's contents; the fish sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The pochard is a diving duck, so it is a species of waterbird.

blocks.note: surface reading: ladies being hugged by noblemen
setter's reading: women included in the House of Lords as members

explanation.walkthrough: The House of Lords is the upper chamber of the UK Parliament; women who are peers sit there in their own right.
explanation.definitionFit: Women holding a title of nobility, entitled to sit in the House of Lords, are female peers.

clue.text: Cricket leaders in the morning crush

indicators.note: leaders in the plural are the front-runners, so the opening pair of letters is kept

blocks.note: the opening two letters of the word
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: The cricket team's captains squeeze in an early practice.
explanation.definitionFit: To cram is to pack or squeeze tightly, much as a crush packs people together.

clue.text: Put off Martian with stewed tea

indicators.note: stewed means cooked down and mixed up, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a Martian is an alien from Mars
taken as written

explanation.surface: A visitor from Mars is offered tea that has stood too long and is disgusted.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to make them hostile or estranged, to repel them.

indicators.note: out here means disordered or not in place, so the letters are reshuffled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vagrant is released from custody clutching a bottle of scrumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a derelict is a vagrant or down-and-out person with no home.

clue.text: Percentage who do it are somewhat backward

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the phrase is used, a run of letters inside it
backward tells us to read that run of letters from right to left

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of do, all of it, and the start of are

explanation.surface: Survey statistics show the share of people who do something is a bit low.
explanation.walkthrough: OITAR, read in reverse, gives RATIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses a proportion between quantities, as a percentage also does.

blocks.note: surface reading: Fishguard, the ferry port in Pembrokeshire, Wales
setter's reading: split as fish plus guard, one word naming a deep-sea fish and a soldier of a Guards regiment

explanation.walkthrough: Fishguard is a ferry port in Wales; the question mark invites splitting it into fish and guard. The Grenadier Guards are a British Army regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a deep-sea fish of the cod order and a soldier of a famous Guards regiment.

indicators.note: something under repair is being taken apart and put back together, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; it does double duty in the indicator

explanation.surface: A farmer has made a broken gate secure while it is being mended.
explanation.definitionFit: Something guaranteed has been made certain or secured, as a loan is secured by collateral.

indicators.note: taking the head off a word drops its first letter

blocks.note: a canal is a duct or tube in anatomy, such as the ear canal

explanation.surface: A fussy plumber decapitates a pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: CANAL loses its first letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: Anal is the informal word for someone excessively fussy about detail, short for anal-retentive.

indicators.note: say flags an example, so the named place stands for a general word for its kind

blocks.note: little in height means short
Victoria Falls on the Zambezi is an example of waterfalls

explanation.surface: A small girl called Victoria has fallen behind with her payments.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortfalls are deficits where money owed is not paid, which is what arrears are.

clue.text: The last word before setter joins services

blocks.note: amen is said at the end of a prayer, the last word
the setter refers to themself as I
ties means links or joins

explanation.surface: A setter caps a church service by ending with the final word of prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenities are useful facilities or services, such as shops and toilets.

blocks.note: first meaning: a weather condition in which snow makes everything look white
second meaning: to cover a mistake with white correction fluid

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a blizzard as an example of the first meaning rather than an exact synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A whiteout is a blizzard with no visibility, and to white out a typing error is to correct it.

blocks.note: kind means nice or pleasant
the ling is a long fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A tasty plate of fish and chips.
explanation.walkthrough: Fish and chips suggests the meal; Nice is not the French city but the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindling is small sticks and wood chips used for lighting a fire.

blocks.note: surface reading: a locksmith's, where door locks are replaced
setter's reading: locks are locks of hair, restyled at a salon

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a locksmith's sign, but the locks are hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon stylist cuts and restyles customers' hair, which is what having your locks changed means.

indicators.note: the prow is the front of a vessel, so the opening letter is taken away

blocks.note: a coracle is a small round Welsh boat of wicker and hide

explanation.surface: A seer damages a boat by taking off its front.
explanation.walkthrough: CORACLE loses its first letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle is someone who gives prophecies, as at Delphi, so is a prophet.

blocks.note: first meaning: to become allies once more
second meaning: truly, as an exclamation of emphasis

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that the first meaning splits the word as re- plus ally.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means truly or in fact, while re-ally is a playful verb for renewing an alliance.

blocks.note: first meaning: considerable in amount
second meaning: neat and in good order

explanation.walkthrough: Spruce suggests the tree, with Large describing it; here it is the adjective meaning smart and neat.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both a sizeable sum of money and something neat, orderly and smart.

indicators.note: letters that are playing are moving about freely, so they can be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to go to the opera, and is told not if a certain instrument is being played.
explanation.definitionFit: The pianoforte is the full name of the piano, a keyboard musical instrument.

clue.text: Proportion of men in the world

indicators.note: in the world here reads as contained within, so the letters sit inside the words before it

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of men through in to the start of the

explanation.surface: A statistic on what fraction of the global population is male.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninth is one of nine equal parts, a fraction or proportion of a whole.

blocks.note: first meaning: plucky and willing
second meaning: wild creatures hunted for sport or food

explanation.walkthrough: Brave animals sounds like courageous beasts, but the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means spirited and ready, and the noun names wild animals hunted for sport or food.

indicators.note: to treat something is to process it, working its letters into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemist recommends a toxic chemical as a remedy for corroded metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rust is iron oxide formed when the metal reacts with oxygen, a chemical process of this kind.

clue.text: Cetacean halts oil spill — pain thereby relieved

indicators.note: a spill scatters material in every direction, so the letters are scattered and reformed

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A whale blocks an oil slick, and the pain of the pollution is eased.
explanation.walkthrough: Cetacean is a whale or dolphin. The definition is a description: this is what relieves pain in one part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug injected to numb one area, as at the dentist, is the means by which pain is relieved.

clue.text: New lead given to stray cat

indicators.note: a new lead means the opening letter of the word is swapped for a different one

blocks.note: to digress is to stray from the subject

explanation.surface: A wandering cat has been fitted with a new leash.
explanation.walkthrough: DIGRESS swaps its first letter D for T. The clue does not say which letter, so the definition and crossings fix it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigress is a female tiger, one of the big cats.

blocks.note: surface reading: laundry hung over clothes pegs on a line
setter's reading: pegs is slang for legs, so these are garments worn on the legs

explanation.walkthrough: Pegs is informal for legs; the surface suggests a washing line.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockings, tights and socks are collectively hosiery, garments that cover the legs.
